QUESTION: What is the suffix array (SA) of a text $T$ of length $n$?

ATOM: The suffix array (SA) of a text $T$ of length $n$ is a permutation of $[0,n)$ such that $T[SA[i],n) < T[SA[j],n)$ for all $0 \le i < j < n$, so it lists all suffixes of $T$ in lexicographic order.
KEY POINTS:
1. A permutation of the indices $[0,n)$
2. Listing the suffixes of $T$ in lexicographic order, i.e. $T[SA[i],n) < T[SA[j],n)$ for $i<j$

ANSWER TO GRADE:
The suffix array of a text \(T\) of length \(n\) is an array containing the starting positions of all suffixes of \(T\), sorted in lexicographic order of those suffixes. Thus, \(SA[i]\) is the starting position of the \(i\)-th lexicographically smallest suffix.
